description: thoth-ipc cross-language ABI — language-neutral source of truth. Structurally validated by abi.schema.json; semantically validated against the deployed C++ by abi/dump_abi.cpp via the `tools/abi` Rust checker; behaviourally validated by the xlang matrix. This is an initial slice (ring layouts + core constants); extend it as the codegen adopts more of the surface.

apple_arm64.description: macOS arm64 — the implemented target; AlignSize = min(64, alignof(max_align_t)) = 8; PSHMNAMLEN = 31

x86_64.description: x86-64 / Linux aarch64 — AlignSize = 16; shm_name_max = 0 (no shortening off macOS)

constants.name: large_msg_cache
constants.description: chunk slots per chunk size (id_pool capacity)

constants.name: chan_ep_mask
constants.description: channel rc_: low 56 = rc bits + internal read-gen

constants.name: syncabi_backend_posix_pthread
constants.description: SyncAbi backend id: posix_pthread (pthread_mutex_t / pthread_cond_t; FreeBSD, QNX and other POSIX)

constants.name: syncabi_backend_apple_mach
constants.description: SyncAbi backend id: apple_mach (App-Store-safe macOS profile; C++ only)

constants.name: syncabi_backend_win32
constants.description: SyncAbi backend id: win32 (named kernel objects, payload size 0)

constants.name: syncabi_backend_linux_a0
constants.description: SyncAbi backend id: linux_a0 (vendored alephzero robust PI futex mutex a0_mtx_t + condition a0_cnd_t; Linux and Android)

constants.name: sync_abi_suffix_mutex
constants.description: cross-process sync sidecar shm-name suffix for a mutex; full name = <channel-name> + this suffix (byte-exact across all ports)

constants.name: sync_abi_suffix_condition
constants.description: cross-process sync sidecar shm-name suffix for a condition variable; full name = <channel-name> + this suffix (byte-exact across all ports)

structs.name: msg_t
structs.description: message framing inside a slot's data_ (msg_t<64,8>)

fields.name: cc_id
fields.description: sender identity (self-message filter)

fields.name: id
fields.description: message id (fragments share it)

fields.name: remain
fields.description: bytes remaining after this fragment

fields.name: storage
fields.description: payload is a storage_id (large-message path)

fields.name: payload
fields.description: payload fragment or storage_id

structs.name: ring_header
structs.description: shared conn_head_base + cache-line-aligned prod_cons head; identical offsets for route and channel (block_ starts at size)

fields.name: cc
fields.description: connection bitmask

fields.name: lc
fields.description: header lock: thoth::spin_lock = atomic<u32> test-and-set on every target (NOT os_unfair_lock; see context/xlang-channel-abi.md §2), 4 bytes

fields.name: constructed
fields.description: DCLP init flag

fields.name: cursor
fields.description: route wt_ / channel ct_ (write cursor / commit index)

fields.name: epoch
fields.description: writer epoch (atomic on channel, plain on route)

structs.name: route_elem
structs.description: single-writer route slot (elem_t<80,AlignSize>): `alignas(AlignSize) byte_t data_[80]` + `atomic<u64> rc_`. AlignSize = min(DataSize, alignof(max_align_t)), so the ALIGNMENT is what makes the slot 88 on the align-8 targets and 96 elsewhere; it is per-target for the same reason the size is, and a port that hardcodes 8 gets the stride wrong off Apple/MSVC

fields.name: data
fields.description: holds a msg_t

fields.name: rc
fields.description: read-counter (bitmask + epoch)

structs.name: channel_elem
structs.description: multi-writer channel slot (adds the f_ct_ commit flag). Same AlignSize story as route_elem, but the size is unaffected: 80 + 8 + 8 is already a multiple of 16

fields.name: data
fields.description: holds a msg_t

fields.name: rc
fields.description: read-counter (3-region packing)

fields.name: f_ct
fields.description: commit flag (~ct published / next-lap free)

fields.name: sender_owner
fields.description: the single sender's owner record: a liveness_slot right after block_ (elem_array's sender_checker). pid 0 = free, -1 = a claim in flight, >0 = the holder, whose start_tok is its start token. Claim: CAS pid (0, or a DEAD holder's pid) -> -1, store start_tok, store pid (release); a live holder or -1 refuses. Release: start_tok = 0, CAS own pid -> 0. See context/xlang-channel-abi.md §2a

structs.name: channel_ring
structs.description: sizeof(elem_array<channel,80,AlignSize>) — ftruncate target; same on both align classes (the f_ct_ flag already makes the slot 96)

structs.name: chunk_info
structs.description: CHUNK_INFO__<size> header: id_pool free list + the pool spin_lock. Chunks start at offset `size` (C++ `this + 1`).

fields.name: next
fields.description: id_pool free-list links, one u8 per slot (max_count = large_msg_cache)

fields.name: cursor
fields.description: id_pool head of the free list; == max_count means empty

fields.name: prepared
fields.description: id_pool prepared_ flag (bool); init() runs once when the pool reads all-zero

fields.name: lock
fields.description: thoth::spin_lock guarding the pool: atomic<u32> test-and-set, 1 = locked, on every target (see context/xlang-channel-abi.md §2)

structs.name: liveness_slot
structs.description: LV_CONN__ owner table entry (32 of them = 512 B)

fields.name: pid
fields.description: owner pid, 0 = free

fields.name: since
fields.description: broadcast receivers: the ring write cursor (route wt_, channel ct_) the owner read just before claiming its connection bit, stored right after the claim (release). Every element the owner must read is at or after it, so a writer reusing an element whose previous position is before `since` treats the owner's mark on it as a previous owner's leftover, not as unread. 0 until a receiver records it (older peers never do: all marks count, as before). See context/xlang-channel-abi.md §9a

fields.name: start_tok
fields.description: process incarnation token (defeats PID reuse)

structs.name: sipc_header
structs.description: secure envelope v1 fixed header (all little-endian)

fields.name: magic
fields.description: "SIPC"

fields.name: ct_size
fields.description: ciphertext size

structs.name: syncabi_stamp
structs.description: sync ABI guard sidecar (6 x u32)

fields.name: primitive_id
fields.description: 1=mutex, 2=condition

fields.name: payload_size
fields.description: byte size of the backend's shared primitive payload, so peers on different backends or layouts refuse to share it: ulock_mutex_size / ulock_cond_size (apple_ulock), a0_mtx_size / a0_cnd_size (linux_a0), sizeof(pthread_mutex_t / pthread_cond_t) (posix_pthread), 12 / 8 (apple_mach), 0 (win32)

structs.name: ulock_mutex
structs.description: apple_ulock mutex payload (C++ platform/apple/mutex.h ulock_mutex_t, Rust platform/apple.rs, Swift, Zig): the lock word is the __ulock_wait/__ulock_wake address (UL_COMPARE_AND_WAIT_SHARED); holder is the owner pid for dead-holder recovery. Followed in shm by C++'s trailing atomic<i32> ref counter (calc_size)

fields.name: state
fields.description: 0 = unlocked, 1 = locked, 2 = locked + waiters. Lock: spin CAS 0->1 (0->2 once the locker has slept), else set 1->2 and __ulock_wait(state, 2); unlock: holder = 0, exchange state 0, __ulock_wake one if it was 2

fields.name: holder
fields.description: pid of the holder, 0 = none (stored after acquiring). A timed lock that times out, or a try_lock that finds the mutex held, checks once whether this pid is dead (kill(pid, 0) == ESRCH) and if so recovers: exchange state 0, holder 0, __ulock_wake all if state was 2, then retries

structs.name: ulock_cond
structs.description: apple_ulock condition payload (C++ platform/apple/condition.h ulock_cond_t, Rust condition.rs AppleCondState, Swift, Zig): a sequence-counter condition variable over __ulock_wait/__ulock_wake

fields.name: seq
fields.description: wake sequence. Wait: read seq under the mutex, waiters += 1, unlock, __ulock_wait(seq, read value), waiters -= 1, relock. Notify/broadcast: seq += 1, then __ulock_wake (one / ULF_WAKE_ALL) if waiters > 0

fields.name: waiters
fields.description: threads currently blocked in __ulock_wait on seq (lets notify skip the syscall)

structs.name: a0_mtx
structs.description: linux_a0 mutex payload: the vendored alephzero a0_mtx_t (C++ platform/linux/a0/mtx.c, Rust platform/linux.rs) - a robust, error-checking, priority-inheriting futex mutex. It "inherits" the kernel's struct robust_list: next must be the first field, and robust_list_head.futex_offset = offset of ftx. LP64 layout (x86_64 / aarch64 Linux). Followed in shm by C++'s trailing atomic<i32> ref counter (calc_size)

fields.name: next
fields.description: robust_list.next: links the mutex into its holder THREAD's kernel robust list (set_robust_list; a process-local address, meaningful only to the holder). Set by the locker after acquiring, unlinked before release, with robust_list_head.list_op_pending = this mutex around both, so the kernel marks ftx FUTEX_OWNER_DIED when the holder dies

fields.name: prev
fields.description: back link used to unlink in O(1); points at the previous held mutex or at the thread's robust_list_head

fields.name: ftx
fields.description: PI futex word: 0 = unlocked, else holder tid (FUTEX_TID_MASK 0x3fffffff) | FUTEX_WAITERS | FUTEX_OWNER_DIED. Lock: CAS 0->tid, else FUTEX_LOCK_PI (absolute CLOCK_REALTIME timeout); OWNER_DIED after acquiring = EOWNERDEAD until made consistent (clear OWNER_DIED). Unlock (owner tid only, else EPERM): CAS tid->0, else FUTEX_UNLOCK_PI; unlocking while OWNER_DIED leaves FUTEX_TID_MASK|FUTEX_OWNER_DIED = not recoverable (ENOTRECOVERABLE)

structs.name: a0_cnd
structs.description: linux_a0 condition payload: the alephzero a0_cnd_t, a u32 futex sequence word whose waiters are requeued onto the paired a0_mtx.ftx by the kernel (priority-inheritance-aware). Followed in shm by C++'s trailing atomic<i32> ref counter (calc_size)

fields.name: seq
fields.description: wake sequence. Wait: read seq, unlock the mutex, FUTEX_WAIT_REQUEUE_PI(seq, read value, &mtx.ftx, absolute CLOCK_MONOTONIC timeout), retried on EINTR; on ETIMEDOUT / EAGAIN re-lock the mutex manually. Signal/broadcast: seq += 1, then FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE_PI(seq, wake 1, requeue 1 / INT_MAX, &mtx.ftx, new seq), re-reading seq on EAGAIN

names.name: ring
names.description: route AND channel ring (distinguished by layout, not name). posix_golden = make_shm_name(golden): the ring name (35 chars) exceeds macOS PSHMNAMLEN=31 so it shortens to /<13 body chars>_<16-hex fnv1a_64 of the /-name>; off macOS it just gets a leading /.

$protocol_note: A field carrying `protocol` runs a coordination algorithm over its bytes that layout cannot express (a lock discipline, a free-list rule). The value names the conformance probe that must reproduce it in every port — see context/abi-consistency-review.md. tools/abi emits abi/protocols.txt from these, and the xlang runner fails if a listed probe has no case.
